name: Residences at Durango
headline: Residences at Durango converts the former Best Western Inn & Suites at 21382 US-160 W in west Durango into 72 apartments and adds 48 new homes in two three-story buildings, 120 homes in all for households at 30% to 60% AMI, developed and owned by TWG Development; it won $1,322,959 a year in 2022 federal 4% credit with $16M of CHFA bonds, and the first tenants moved into the motel units on 2025-07-11.
why_it_matters: Billed as Colorado's first hotel-to-apartments conversion financed with housing tax credits, it shows both the model (city and nonprofit site control, federal earmark, state grant) and its risks: a hidden water main and a property manager walking away delayed move-ins by about six months.

status.label: Partly open: 72 converted motel units leasing since July 2025; the 48 new-build units not confirmed complete; 8609s not yet issued
status.detail: The first tenant moved in on 2025-07-11 after the city's building division passed final inspection of the motel units; at that point the new buildings had no projected completion date. No public record found confirms completion of the 48 new units, and CHFA still lists the deal on its 2026-09-21 award report, which excludes developments with 8609s issued.

next_step: Watch the City of Durango for a certificate of occupancy on the two new buildings and for 8609 issuance.

background.text: In August 2021 the city put down $70,000 of earnest money on the Best Western, which was listed at $7M for a 5.3-acre hotel parcel plus a 56.5-acre hillside parcel; the city said its aim was to act as a conduit, not the long-term owner.

Durango City Council approved a sale and purchase agreement with TWG Acquisitions in February 2022, with acquisition and development then priced at $30M; the city and Project Moxie bought the property and TWG later reimbursed them.
Construction started after a groundbreaking on 2023-10-27; the original goal was completion by the end of 2024 or early 2025.

Move-ins slipped about six months because crews could not locate a water main where city documents showed it, which held up plumbing, fire and final inspections; the first property manager, Ross-Envolve, pulled out in mid-May 2025, reportedly over nonpayment, and TWG hired Elmington.
The city counts the project toward its Proposition 123 commitment of 184 affordable homes by the end of 2026.
The deal does not appear in CHFA's 2022 Round One or Round Two competitive application narratives; it was a rolling 4% bond deal only.

CHFA's 4% award report says it leaves out developments whose IRS Form 8609s have been issued; this deal is still listed on the 2026-09-21 report, so 8609s had not been issued by then (inferred from the report's note).
